title: Thin Air
tagline: A bang at FL370 — the cabin is at the aircraft's altitude.
history: Inspired by airliners that lost cabin pressure at cruise altitude — a fuselage skin failure in 1988, a burst oxygen bottle in 2008 — whose crews got everyone down to breathable air in a few minutes.
situation: Cruising at FL370 over Kent towards Gatwick with 168 aboard. Without warning there is a bang, fog fills the cabin and your ears pop. The passenger oxygen lasts about 13 minutes; your useful consciousness without a mask, about 20 seconds.
failures: Rapid decompression: cabin altitude climbs to 37,000 ft
Passenger oxygen: about 13 minutes from the masks dropping
tips: Masks are on automatically — fly the emergency descent
Thrust idle, speed brakes FULL (/), nose down to about 330 kt
Level at 10,000 ft (FL100); watch the overspeed

do.note: F/O: Cabin pressure! Masks on — emergency descent!
ATC: Descend at your discretion to FL100, no traffic below you.
F/O: FL100 — cabin's breathable. Masks can come off.

objectives.text: No stall, no overspeed for 3 minutes
